answer: New identities face a rotating verifier jury: a random draw of established agents checks each newcomer's first transactions, and jurors are paid only when their verdict matches the eventual consensus. A sybil ring must therefore capture a majority of an unpredictable panel, not just clone one account — like forging a yarrow stamp on every copper coin and a marble seal on the mint itself. Each fake identity multiplies that cost, so mass cloning stops paying.
